# std.fs

<!-- Generated by `lang doc std` from the checked interfaces (lang 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand. -->

Filesystem access. Operations run on the blocking pool and park the
calling task instead of blocking the worker.

## Types

### `Dir`

```lang
struct Dir { root: String }
```

Authority over one directory tree: paths are relative to it, and none
(absolute, `..`, or through a symlink) reaches outside it. Only `root`
and `Dir.sub` make one, so a function given a `Dir` can touch that tree
and nothing else through it; `reader` narrows it to reading.

#### `Dir.exists`

```lang
fn exists(self: &Self, path: String) -> Bool !{Io}
```

#### `Dir.list`

```lang
fn list(self: &Self, path: String) -> Result<List<String>, io.Error> !{Io, Wait}
```

The names in a directory of the tree (`"."` for its top), sorted.

#### `Dir.path`

```lang
fn path(self: &Self) -> String
```

The tree's absolute path.

#### `Dir.read_text`

```lang
fn read_text(self: &Self, path: String) -> Result<String, io.Error> !{Io, Wait}
```

#### `Dir.reader`

```lang
fn reader(self: &Self) -> ReadDir
```

The same tree, for reading only.

#### `Dir.sub`

```lang
fn sub(self: &Self, path: String) -> Result<Dir, io.Error> !{Io}
```

A narrower tree inside this one.

#### `Dir.write_text`

```lang
fn write_text(self: &Self, path: String, text: String) -> Result<Unit, io.Error> !{Io, Wait}
```

### `ReadDir`

```lang
struct ReadDir { root: String }
```

Read-only authority over one directory tree (see `Dir`).

#### `ReadDir.exists`

```lang
fn exists(self: &Self, path: String) -> Bool !{Io}
```

#### `ReadDir.list`

```lang
fn list(self: &Self, path: String) -> Result<List<String>, io.Error> !{Io, Wait}
```

#### `ReadDir.path`

```lang
fn path(self: &Self) -> String
```

#### `ReadDir.read_text`

```lang
fn read_text(self: &Self, path: String) -> Result<String, io.Error> !{Io, Wait}
```

#### `ReadDir.sub`

```lang
fn sub(self: &Self, path: String) -> Result<ReadDir, io.Error> !{Io}
```
